correctness.rationale: Omitting one of the k+1 agents yields exact weights P/g1 and P/gk for end omissions and P(1/g_j+1/g_{j+1}) for an interior omission, where P=product g_i, and realized omitted distances are g1, gk, or min(g_j,g_{j+1}). Sum weights 2P sum g_i^-1 and costs P[k+1+sum adjacent min/max]. At least two of k+1 agents share one of k arbitrary facility locations, so triangle inequality gives OPT>=minimum gap; placing one facility at each remaining report attains that bound. Every omitted agent has positive selection probability, so C=OPT iff every omission is cost-minimal. For an index with minimal gap m, any neighboring ratio u=m/g_neighbor>0 yields C/m<= (2k-1+u)/(2(1+u))<k-1/2. Family (1,T,...,T) tends to k-1/2. Independently enumerated every omission with exact Fraction arithmetic for k=2..5 and gaps in {1,2,3,4}^k (1360 profiles), reproducing the identities and boundaries. Coincident sites have OPT=0 and ratio undefined; not part of the ratio statement.

final_claim: For exactly n=k+1 strictly ordered agents and k>=2 facilities sampled from reports with probability proportional to the product of successive selected gaps, C_k(g)=[k+1+sum_i min(g_i,g_{i+1})/max(g_i,g_{i+1})]/[2 sum_i 1/g_i], OPT_k=min_i g_i, 1<=C/OPT<k-1/2 with unattained sharp supremum k-1/2; equality C=OPT iff both endpoint gaps minimal and every consecutive pair contains a minimal gap.
